proposal.description: The cycle-boundary increment takes priority over the synchronous clear, so a bad rail or a departure from S_RUN on the clock that pwm_fall fires advances the qualifying counter instead of restarting it
proposal.reason: If a one-clock comparator dip (or run_active drop) lands on the pwm_fall clock, the original restarts the count but the mutant increments it. PGOOD then asserts after a good period that was not continuous, earlier than PGOOD_DELAY_CYCLES consecutive good cycles after the dip.

proposal.description: The qualifying counter is restarted only while it is still qualifying; once at TARGET, a comparator dip or exit from S_RUN leaves it saturated, as though the live gating on PGOOD were enough
proposal.reason: After PGOOD has asserted, pgood_comp drops (or run_active drops) and then comes back. The original keeps PGOOD low for a fresh PGOOD_DELAY_CYCLES qualifying period, but the mutant raises PGOOD again on the first clock the conditions return.

proposal.description: The qualifying counter saturates at its all-ones value (as the package comment describes) instead of at TARGET, so it runs past the count PGOOD compares against
proposal.reason: With the default PGOOD_DELAY_CYCLES not equal to 2**PGOOD_DELAY_W-1, the counter passes TARGET on the next switching-cycle boundary. PGOOD goes high for one switching cycle and then drops for good, even though the rail stays good in S_RUN.

proposal.description: PGOOD treats the counter's top bit as the 'qualified' flag instead of comparing it with TARGET
proposal.reason: With the default delay, TARGET is not a power of two, so the MSB sets at 2**(PGOOD_DELAY_W-1) cycles. PGOOD then asserts before the full PGOOD_DELAY_CYCLES consecutive good cycles have passed in S_RUN.
